To estimate the causal effect of higher household income on health, I will employ an instrumental variable (IV) approach using the random assignment of the unconditional cash transfer program as my instrument. The treatment will be the log of household income per adult equivalent, while the outcome will be the number of illness episodes reported in the past four weeks prior to the interview. The key variables in this analysis include the transfer_draw variable, which indicates whether a household's village was selected for the cash transfer, and the baseline covariates such as age, gender, and education to control for potential confounding effects. The main threat to validity concerns the possibility of unobserved factors that could influence both income and health, particularly if individuals in drawn villages differ systematically from those in non-drawn villages beyond just the cash transfer. The treatment effect will be identified by comparing changes in health outcomes between households in treatment and control villages while accounting for fixed effects related to individual characteristics and survey rounds.
